article.title: Why Teams Use a Parking Lot in Meetings
article.author: OpenAI learning editor
article.why: 用簡單英文學會如何在會議中保護議程，又不漏掉重要的延伸問題。

paragraphs.en:
A meeting can easily move away from its main purpose. Someone mentions a useful idea, another person asks a related question, and suddenly the group spends fifteen minutes on a topic that was not part of the plan. The discussion may be important, but it can also prevent the team from finishing the work it came to do.

One simple tool is a meeting parking lot. A parking lot is a short list of topics that are important but do not need to be solved immediately. When a side topic appears, the facilitator writes it down and tells the group when it will be discussed later. This allows people to feel heard without losing the current agenda.

For example, a project meeting may be focused on next week's launch. Someone raises a question about a future reporting dashboard. The question matters, but the launch decision is more urgent. Instead of ignoring the idea or starting a long discussion, the team adds “reporting dashboard requirements” to the parking lot and continues with the launch plan.

A good parking lot needs follow-up. At the end of the meeting, the team should review the list and decide what happens next. Some items may need a separate meeting. Others can be answered by email or assigned to one person. If the list is never reviewed, it becomes a place where ideas disappear.

The parking lot is not a way to avoid difficult topics. It is a way to protect focus while keeping useful issues visible. Used well, it gives the group permission to say, “This matters, but not right now.” That small habit can make meetings shorter, clearer, and more respectful of everyone's time. It also creates a useful record of what the team intentionally postponed. Over time, recurring parking-lot items can reveal unclear ownership, missing decisions, or topics that deserve their own regular forum. In that sense, the list is not only a meeting tool; it can also show where the team's normal process needs improvement.
paragraphs.zh: 會議很容易偏離原本目的：有人提出有用想法，另一個人接著追問，團隊可能花十五分鐘討論不在原定議程中的事情。Meeting parking lot 是一個簡單工具，把『重要、但現在不用立即解決』的議題先記錄下來。主持人把延伸問題放進清單，讓大家知道之後會處理，這樣既不忽略發言，也不破壞目前議程。例如會議正在處理下週上線，有人提出未來報表 dashboard 的需求，就可以先放入 parking lot，再繼續完成上線決策。Parking lot 不能只是把問題丟進去，會議結束前還要確認哪些項目需要另外開會、用郵件回答或指派 owner。它不是逃避困難議題，而是保護焦點，同時保留重要問題。長期觀察重複出現的項目，還能發現責任不清、缺少決策機制或需要固定討論場域的流程問題。
paragraphs.ja: 会議は簡単に本来の目的から外れます。誰かが有用なアイデアを出し、別の人が関連質問をすると、予定外の話題に十五分使ってしまうことがあります。Meeting parking lot は『重要だが今すぐ解く必要はない話題』を短く記録する仕組みです。進行役が横道の話題を書き留め、後で扱うことを伝えることで、発言を無視せず現在のagendaを守れます。たとえば来週のlaunchを決める会議で将来のreporting dashboardが話題になった場合、parking lotに入れてlaunch判断を先に終えます。最後には各項目を別会議、メール、担当者への割当などへつなげます。Parking lotは難しい問題を避けるためではなく、focusを守りながら重要事項を見える状態にする方法です。繰り返し出る項目は、ownership不足や意思決定プロセスの問題を示すこともあります。

quiz.question: Why is a meeting parking lot useful?
quiz.answer: It protects the agenda while keeping important side topics visible.
